newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARLINS SIGN FREE AGENT OF MOISES ALOU.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARLINS SIGN FREE AGENT OF MOISES ALOU.

text.p: The Florida Marlins came out winners in the free agent sweepstakes again on Thursday with the signing of outfielder Moises Alou, who had been with the Montreal Expos.
Alou, who last season batted .281 with 21 homers, 96 RBI and 87 runs scored while playing for his father, Montreal manager Felipe Alou, agreed to a five-year contract reportedly worth $25 million.
The Marlins have been one of the most active teams in the free agent market this off-season.

Florida on Monday gave former Chicago White Sox pitcher Alex Fernandez a five-year deal reportedly worth $35 million. The Marlins signed Bobby Bonilla to a four-year, $23 million contract last month and also signed outfielders Jim Eisenreich and John Cangelosi as free agents.
"I was a little worried when they signed all those guys there would not be enough money for me," joked Alou. "I'm happy to be a Florida Marlin."

Like Fernandez, Alou was granted his free agency as a result of Major Legue Baseball's new collective bargaining agreement. The 30-year-old left fielder was declared a free agent when players were granted lost service time for the baseball strike in the newly-ratified agreement.
Alou was an All-Star in the strike-shortened 1994 season when he batted .339 with 22 homers and 78 RBI.
Alou was originally selected by the Pittsburgh Pirates in the first round of the June 1986 draft and was traded to Montreal September 1, 1990.
